description: `accounts trip <pool> --kind budget` writes breaker-state.json for real (no automatic reset — a human must run `accounts reset`, deliberately chosen over --kind rolling/weekly so the scenario needs no clock-dependent reset_at in its expected text); a later `dispatch --dry-run` against a chain whose first seat shares that pool reads the trip as a pure file check (accounts.py's `_availability` check 4, no herdr call) and falls back to the second seat with the exact breaker wording in its skip reason.

home.config_toml:
[accounts.seat-a]
kind = "codex"
short = "sa"
config_dir_var = "CODEX_HOME"
config_dir = "{{DIR:codex-home-a}}"
pool = "codex:solo"

[accounts.seat-b]
kind = "codex"
short = "sb"
config_dir_var = "CODEX_HOME"
config_dir = "{{DIR:codex-home-b}}"
pool = "codex:other"

[projects.sandbox]
path = "{{PROJECT:sandbox}}"

[projects.sandbox.chains]
explorer = ["seat-a", "seat-b"]

[roles.explorer]
write_scope = "none"
effort = "low"
on_exhausted = "degrade"
skills = []

[roles.explorer.models]
codex = "gpt-test"

stdout_contains: skipped     seat-a: breaker open for pool 'codex:solo': no automatic reset — a human has to resolve this and run `accounts reset`
